paper_metadata.title: Feature Ranking in Credit-Risk with Qudit-Based Networks

summary: The paper studies a single-qudit variational QNN for Taiwan credit-risk classification on 30,000 records with 23 features and d=5. It reports clean-data macro-F1 of 0.667 ± 0.015 and poisoned-data F1 of 0.632 ± 0.040, but the classical neural network is better on clean F1 at 0.682 ± 0.011 and random forest is stronger on poisoned interpretability (WIS 0.953 ± 0.026 vs 0.853 ± 0.048 for the QNN).

experiments.description: Single-qudit variational quantum neural network for credit-risk classification on the Taiwan credit card default dataset, evaluated for predictive performance, feature-ranking interpretability, and robustness under feature poisoning.

algorithm.variant: single-qudit QNN with Hamiltonian co-encoding of data and trainable weights; multilayer data re-uploading
algorithm.ansatz: unitary layers of the form exp(-i sum_j h(x_j w_j^(l)) G_j) over su(d) generators
algorithm.convergence_criteria: training stopped when validation error improvement saturated

problem_formulation.encoding_details: classical features x_j and trainable weights w_j are co-encoded into coefficients of su(d) generators in a single-qudit Hamiltonian; no qubit-based amplitude/angle/basis encoding is used
problem_formulation.objective_function: binary credit-risk classification minimizing cross-entropy with L2 regularization
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: L2 regularization; no explicit hard constraints

problem_instance.description: Credit-risk prediction / default classification for Taiwan credit card clients
problem_instance.dataset_name: Default of Credit Card Clients (Taiwan credit card default dataset)

dataset_specification.description: UCI Machine Learning Repository; 30,000 records; binary target default/non-default; 23 input attributes

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: features rescaled; products x_j w_j remapped through h(z)=2 arctan(2z); in poisoning evaluation, 7 randomly selected features replaced with Gaussian noise during inference
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10 runs with different random seeds; compared on uncorrupted data and on poisoned data; metrics include macro-F1, edit distance to LR feature ranking, and WIS

implementation_details.classical_solver: Adam optimizer; classical baselines include LR, RF, and NN
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: feature ranking from learned weights; edit-distance comparison to LR; WIS computation; performance aggregation over runs

speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic or runtime speedup claim is made; the paper reports empirical predictive performance and parameter efficiency only.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Single-qudit numerical simulation; no hardware resource estimate or asymptotic speedup analysis provided.
limiting_factors: Classical neural network achieves higher clean-data F1 (0.682 vs 0.667)
Random forest is competitive or better on interpretability metrics in poisoned setting (WIS 0.953 vs 0.853)
No runtime, scaling, or crossover analysis
Simulation-only study with no QPU execution

notes: hardware.type inferred as simulator_other because the paper reports a numerical/simulation study with no physical QPU or vendor device named.
num_qubits reported as d=5 qudit dimension; mapped to 5-level logical register size for extraction purposes.
circuit depth is not explicitly quantified; only multilayer structure is described.

Classical NN outperforms the qudit QNN on clean-data F1, while RF is stronger on poisoned-data WIS.

experiments.description: Single-qudit variational quantum neural network for credit-risk classification on the Taiwan credit card default dataset, evaluated on both clean and feature-poisoned data.

algorithm.variant: single-qudit QNN with Hamiltonian co-encoding and multilayer data re-uploading

key_results: Classical baselines: LR 0.601 ± 0.006 clean F1, RF 0.647 ± 0.008 clean F1, NN 0.682 ± 0.011 clean F1
Poisoned-data baselines: LR 0.579 ± 0.020 F1, RF 0.614 ± 0.027 F1, LR WIS 0.932 ± 0.043, RF WIS 0.953 ± 0.026
